tickerText: [TENNIS] North American hard-court season begins as the Mubadala DC Open main draw starts in Washington with Alex Eala facing Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen • [SQUASH] India's junior teams surge at the World Team Championships as the men top Group 5 and the women beat Chinese Taipei • [BADMINTON] Chou Tien Chen becomes the oldest Super 1000 champion at 36, beating Toma Junior Popov to win the China Open in Changzhou • [PICKLEBALL] Wong Hong Kit claims his third straight PPA Asia men's singles title at the inaugural Singapore Open while Long Yufei sweeps women's singles and doubles • [TABLE TENNIS] Hugo Calderano ends a year-long drought with WTT Star Contender glory in São José dos Campos, edging Alexis Lebrun 4-3 in a seven-set final

newsItems.title: DC Open Kicks Off Hard-Court Swing
newsItems.excerpt: The Mubadala DC Open main draw begins today in Washington as Alex Eala draws Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen in the first round of the North American hard-court season.

newsItems.title: India Juniors Advance in Canada
newsItems.excerpt: India's men's junior team topped Group 5 with 3-0 wins over the Netherlands and Brazil, while the women opened with a 3-0 victory over Chinese Taipei in Niagara-on-the-Lake.

newsItems.title: Chou Makes Super 1000 History
newsItems.excerpt: At 36, Chou Tien Chen became the oldest BWF Super 1000 champion by beating Toma Junior Popov 21-15, 7-21, 21-13 in the China Open final in Changzhou.

newsItems.title: Calderano Ends Title Drought
newsItems.excerpt: Hugo Calderano rallied from two sets down to beat Alexis Lebrun 4-3 and win the WTT Star Contender São José dos Campos, his first circuit title in a year.
